culprits: Norah Burton (Mrs. Pomfret, Mrs. Spencer, Stella Keane)
surface_summary: A man is found dead in a locked house in Cathcart Square with a slit throat and a razor in his hand, initially ruled a suicide and identified as Reginald Davis, a fugitive accused of murder. Suspicion arises when the real Reginald Davis reappears alive, and investigations reveal the victim to be Major Hugh Murchison, murdered by a criminal couple who staged the death to look like Davis's suicide.
accepted_facts: A man was found dead in No. 10 Cathcart Square with a slit throat and a razor in his hand.
The dead man was initially identified as Reginald Davis, a fugitive accused of murder.
Reginald Davis was later found alive and well, proving the dead man was misidentified.
Major Hugh Murchison disappeared around the time of the murder and was later identified as the victim.
inferred_conclusions: The death was a suicide by Reginald Davis due to fear of capture.
Norah Burton was an innocent woman unaware of the murder.
George Burton was a respectable stockbroker unrelated to the crime.
mechanism_description: Norah Burton and George Burton murdered Major Hugh Murchison to prevent him from exposing their criminal past. They used the victim's resemblance to Reginald Davis to forge letters and stage the murder as Davis's suicide. They gained entry to the empty house by breaking a window pane and incapacitated Murchison before killing him and placing the razor in his hand to simulate suicide.
delivery_path: Norah Burton and George Burton planned to eliminate Major Hugh Murchison.
They broke a pane of glass in the scullery window of No. 10 Cathcart Square to gain entry.
The caretaker was given a holiday to avoid disturbance during the murder.
Norah used a stupefying agent to incapacitate Murchison during their meeting.
George Burton slit Murchison's throat while he was incapacitated.
They placed a razor in the victim's hand to simulate suicide.
They planted forged letters addressed to Reginald Davis to mislead investigators.
outcome_result: Norah Burton and George Burton commit suicide to avoid arrest after their crime is uncovered.

false_assumption.statement: The dead man in Cathcart Square was Reginald Davis who committed suicide out of fear of capture.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The body was found with letters addressed to Reginald Davis and identified by his sister, supported by a forged suicide note. The victim's resemblance to Davis reinforced this belief.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: The victim was actually Major Hugh Murchison, murdered and disguised as Davis to mislead the police. The identification was a deliberate deception by the culprits.

supporting_points: Broken window pane suggested forced entry.
Caretaker was absent during the murder.
Caretaker had a weak character and was suspected of lying.
Caretaker had no alibi for the night.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: Miles had a solid alibi supported by witnesses and was not involved in the crime.

red_herrings.description: Caretaker Miles was suspected due to his absence and broken window but had a credible alibi.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Miles was on holiday with a friend and had no involvement in the murder.

red_herrings.description: Jack Pomfret's suicide was initially thought to be related to the murder mystery.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Pomfret's suicide was due to despair after discovering Norah's criminal past, not the murder itself.

suspects: Norah Burton (Mrs. Pomfret, Mrs. Spencer, Stella Keane)
closed_circle.rationale: Only these individuals had plausible access to the empty house and motive; Miles was cleared by alibi, leaving Norah and George as the only eligible culprits.

time_windows: murder time between caretaker's holiday and discovery

inference_path.observation: Body found with letters addressed to Reginald Davis and a suicide note in his name
inference_path.correction: Reginald Davis was later found alive, so the letters and note were planted
inference_path.effect: The identity of the dead man is questioned
required_evidence: Letters addressed to Reginald Davis found on the body

inference_path.observation: Caretaker Miles was absent and window broken
inference_path.correction: Miles had a credible alibi supported by witnesses
required_evidence: Miles's alibi testimony from friend at Shepperton
Testimony of constables Brown and younger colleague

inference_path.observation: Norah Burton's close association with known criminals and suspicious behavior
inference_path.correction: Detective Bryant confirms Norah Burton is the same person as Stella Keane
inference_path.effect: Norah identified as a suspect with criminal past
required_evidence: Detective Bryant's identification of Norah Burton as Stella Keane
Surveillance reports of meetings between Norah and George Burton

inference_path.observation: George Burton operates a bucket-shop and has a criminal record
inference_path.correction: George Burton is confirmed as the same person as George Dutton
required_evidence: Detective Bryant's identification of George Dutton as George Burton
City office records of George Dutton

inference_path.observation: Major Hugh Murchison disappeared suddenly and belongings left at station
inference_path.correction: Body exhumed and identified as Major Murchison, not Reginald Davis
inference_path.effect: Victim identity confirmed as Murchison, confirming murder
required_evidence: Exhumation and identification of body by multiple witnesses including Guy Spencer
Hotel manager's testimony about Murchison's departure

inference_path.observation: Diary found in victim's luggage detailing events leading to murder
inference_path.correction: Diary entries implicate Norah and George in murder plot
inference_path.effect: Strong evidence against Norah and George
required_evidence: Diary entries recovered from victim's luggage

inference_path.observation: Surveillance shows Norah and George meeting clandestinely and exchanging envelopes
inference_path.correction: Envelope exchanges likely payments or bribes related to crime
required_evidence: Witness statements of meetings at City restaurants

discriminating_test.design: Detectives monitor Norah Burton and George Dutton's movements and meetings, verifying if they can meet only under conditions consistent with conspiracy. They also verify the caretaker's absence and window break timing to confirm access. The exhumed body is identified by multiple witnesses to confirm victim identity.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The test reveals that Norah and George had opportunity and motive, and that the victim was Major Murchison, not Reginald Davis.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Identification of the exhumed body as Major Murchison and confirmed clandestine meetings between Norah and George prove their guilt.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given all key facts: the broken window, the caretaker's absence and alibi, the forged letters, the reappearance of Reginald Davis, the suspicious behavior of Norah and George, and the diary found with the victim. The false identification and planted evidence are clearly presented. The detective's reasoning and surveillance are described in detail, allowing the reader to deduce the true identity of the victim and the culprits' method.
